The structural rewrite that replaces a refuting subgraph with a single canonical 'defeater' node violates the determinism of the fixed point because it admits non-confluent rewrites under arbitrary refutation orderings, a flaw the target itself acknowledges as unproven. If applying rewrites in different orders yields distinct normalized graphs, the resulting grounded extensions will differ, destroying the determinism guarantee required by the problem context.

Change the skeptical semantics from a least fixed point of a monotone operator to the unique model of a nonmonotone logic program with explicit defeat rules, and prove that this model coincides with the grounded extension on acyclic attack graphs but differs on cycles by treating odd-length cycles as refuting all members and even-length cycles as suspending all. This makes odd cycles refuted rather than suspended, retaining determinism and polynomial cost via stratification, but it abandons standard reinstatement on cyclic graphs, so it is a deliberate trade-off.

Replace the skeptical fixed-point label function with a dialectical game: Proponent claims a node, Opponent attacks with warrant-carriages, Proponent replies with an accepted counterattack; acceptance is existence of a winning strategy in a finite game. The grounded extension is then the set of nodes with a winning strategy that does not depend on order of play. Reinstatement becomes a game-theoretic derived property and the strategy tree is a natural certificate, but the game is only polynomial if restricted to DAG attacks or bounded repetition; otherwise PSPACE-hardness threatens.

Parameterize the grounded extension by a school policy that selects which warrant-carriages count as attack edges, and make the skeptical fixpoint return not a single extension but a compact representation of the family of extensions as the policy ranges over a finite policy lattice. Determinism is preserved per policy, the policy-dependent function becomes auditable, and cost stays polynomial if the lattice has bounded width. Criticizable because the family may not be monotone in the policy order, so the compact representation may degrade to a full truth table.

Add a compositional interface: define an operation that combines two grounded-extension graphs by identifying a set of shared committed roots, and prove that the grounded extension of the union is the least fixed point of the combined operator and equals the join of the individual extensions when they agree on the shared roots. This enables modular expansion across schools while preserving determinism and root validity.

Add a parameterized trust threshold over attack edges: each edge carries a warrant strength (direct evidence, inferential, conjectural); for any threshold t, compute the grounded extension on the subgraph of edges with strength >= t. Prove the family is monotone in t, each extension is deterministic and polynomial, and committed roots remain valid because only edges are filtered, never added. This gives a principled way to expand skepticism by choosing t without changing the fixpoint operator.

Introduce a dynamic re-computation protocol that, after an edge insertion or deletion, updates the grounded statuses incrementally by reusing the previous least fixpoint, with a change-propagation order that provably reaches the same fixpoint in polynomial total time. This makes the semantics responsive to new evidence without recomputing from scratch, and preserves determinism because the incremental result is defined as the unique least fixpoint of the updated graph.

Require every accepted node to carry a constructive grounded derivation certificate — a finite tree of attack/defense edges whose leaves are committed roots and whose internal nodes are IN by the grounded rules. The certificate is produced as a side output of the fixpoint and can be independently verified in polynomial time. This strengthens trust in committed roots without altering the semantics.

For every UNDECIDED node, compute its suspension margin: the minimum number of attack-edge deletions that would make it accepted under grounded semantics, using a polynomial-time sensitivity oracle over the final fixpoint rather than bounded-depth lookahead. This turns the binary suspension state into a graded diagnostic without promoting any node, thereby preserving the skeptical semantics and all guarantees.

Define a refutation witness for each REFUTED node: a finite set of attacking chains such that no grounded defense can exist, certified by the absence of an IN defender at the fixpoint and by a monotone invariant that blocks any later reinstatement. This makes refutations checkable and supports a stronger external audit trail while preserving the existing fixpoint.

Prove an impossibility boundary: any monotone edge-construction enrichment that preserves determinism, polynomial cost, and committed-root validity cannot increase the set of accepted conjectures beyond the original grounded extension; therefore the only responsible strengthening is to enrich the vocabulary of defeat, e.g., typed attacks with side conditions, rather than the graph. Criticizable because the proof may rely on a too-restrictive definition of edge-construction and miss enrichment via annotations or proof certificates.

Adopt a proof-theoretic grounding: define acceptance by existence of a canonical, polynomial-time-checkable dialectical proof tree whose leaves are committed roots, and treat the fixed-point labeling only as a sanity check. This changes the semantics from a global fixed point to a local proof search. Criticizable because proof-tree existence may not be monotone under edge addition unless the tree language is carefully restricted, and it may reintroduce self-support if cycles are not handled explicitly.

Use a semiring of evidence, e.g., tropical or fuzzy, to assign each attack a weight and each defense a contribution; acceptance is determined by solving a polynomial-time system of equations over the semiring, with the grounded extension as the least solution. This generalizes integer weights but changes the algebraic structure. Criticizable because the choice of semiring is not uniquely justified and may make reinstatement non-structural or require an additional fixpoint that breaks polynomial cost.

Introduce a commitment-root validity oracle: require every accepted node to have a shortest defense path to a committed root, and strengthen acceptance by requiring the path to be witness-minimal under a polynomial-time canonical ordering. This gives a graded notion of commitment and makes reinstatement a property of path-minimality. Criticizable because shortest paths may not capture argumentative reinstatement, and the canonical ordering may be manipulable by adding redundant defense paths.

Strengthen the grounded extension by adding an explicit defeat-priority total order over attacks, computed by a canonical polynomial-time rule. A node is accepted if it is defended against all higher-priority attackers, and reinstatement becomes a consequence of priority order rather than an emergent property. Criticizable because any priority order introduces arbitrary tie-breaking that may not reflect evidence strength, and the rule may be manipulable by synthetic edge ordering.

Make the grounded extension robust to future evidence by computing, in polynomial time, a suspension region of nodes whose status would change under any single edge addition; these nodes are labelled SUSPENDED-REVISABLE and the fixed point is augmented with this region as a derived annotation. Criticizable because sensitivity analysis may require examining all possible edge additions and could become exponential unless restricted to local perturbations, and the annotation may not be stable across graph revisions.
